articles.content: CHENNAI BADMINTON Mahimkar bags double; Spruha, Anvisha win Greater Mumbai’s Harshit Mahimkar completed a notable double, claiming the men’s singles and boys under-19 singles titles at the Bombay Gymkhana presents Yonex Sunrise Bombay Gymkhana Maharashtra State Open Badminton Tournament. He then lived up to his status as the top seed in the boys under-19 category, beating Palghar’s 6th seed Ruturaj Chipat 15-9, 15-5. Unseeded Spruha Joshi of Mumbai Suburban, continuing her good form, showed nerve to recover from losing the first game and beat Greater Mumbai’s Anvisha Ghorpade 12-15, 15-6, 16-14 to win the girls under-19 title. Anvisha, however, had some consolation, as she won the under-17 final, beating Imaan Motorala 15-9, 15-7. All five individual events were in action on day one. In Mixed Doubles, Prince and Ishita Negi won 15-9, 13-15, 16-14 against Bhashy Pathak and Siona Gala, while Amith Raj Natraj and Suhina Roy beat Sanidhya Sunil Ekade and Yutika Chavan 15-9, 15-9. With maximum power reaching 600kW, the new generation of cars will deliver performance approaching 804bhp, with a top speed of 208mph (335km/h) and acceleration from 0-100km/h in just 1.8 seconds. World No. 38, Senthilkumar, who won a second PSA Copper-level title of his career at the Czech Open earlier this month, beat his opponent 11-4, 11-7, 11-4 in the second round after receiving an opening-round bye. Second seed Senthilkumar will meet Egyptian world No. 80 and fifth seed Omar Said next. articles.title: Prince William, Princess Kate get taste of Mumbai street food with Sachin Tendulkar - India Today
articles.summary: Prince William, Princess Kate get taste of Mumbai street food with Sachin Tendulkar India Today
articles.content: Prince William and Princess Kate had a familiar face for company as they explored the streets of Mumbai, with cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar joining the royal couple for a walk through the city. The trio were spotted together outside Hamilton Studios, one of India's oldest photography studios, before taking in some of Mumbai's street food, including a cutting chai, and local flavour.The meeting brought together Britain's future king and queen with one of India's most celebrated sporting icons. William and Kate arrived in Mumbai on Monday for a three-day visit to India, with Tendulkar among the prominent personalities expected to be part of their engagements in the city. The royal couple were seen walking alongside Tendulkar through Ballard Estate, getting a glimpse of Mumbai beyond its usual tourist attractions. The visit also included a taste of the city's street food, adding a relaxed, informal touch to an otherwise high-profile trip.And, inevitably, there was cricket. Kate later tried her hand at gully cricket, taking a few swings as children stationed close to the batter waited to catch the ball.But both Kate and William lost their wickets, prompting the Princess of Wales to admit with a smile: "I think we need some more practice, so next time!"The couple's cricket connection with Mumbai dates back to April 2016, when they played street cricket with local children during their first official visit to India. A decade later, the city has brought them back to the game, this time with Tendulkar, one of its most celebrated sporting icons, alongside them. William and Kate's Mumbai engagements extend beyond sport, with the couple also expected to take a ride on the city's Metro rail and interact with personalities from Bollywood. They will attend the Earthshot Prize ceremony on Tuesday before travelling to New Delhi, where they are scheduled to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday.WHY ARE PRINCE WILLIAM AND PRINCESS KATE IN MUMBAI?The Prince and Princess of Wales are in India for the sixth edition of the Earthshot Prize, an environmental initiative founded by William in 2020 to identify and support innovative solutions to the planet's biggest challenges. Five winners will receive Â£1 million each to scale up their projects, with this year's ceremony being the biggest edition of the awards so far.The Mumbai programme will highlight the longstanding cultural connections between India and the UK through cricket, fashion and cinema. Bollywood personalities, including Alia Bhatt, are among those expected at the awards ceremony, while British pop group Take That are also scheduled to perform.The visit is particularly significant for Kate, marking her most high-profile overseas engagement since undergoing preventative chemotherapy in 2024. The couple's previous official visit to India was in April 2016, when they also travelled to Bhutan.Beyond the awards, the visit is intended to highlight growing cooperation between India and the UK in clean energy, sustainable transport, innovation and trade. Their final engagement will be a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, bringing the three-day visit to a close.- Ends

articles.content: CHENNAI BADMINTON Karnataka boys, Tamil Nadu girls crowned champions in 49th Junior Team Championships Karnataka boys and Tamil Nadu girls were crowned champions in the 49th Junior National Badminton Championships with comfortable 2-0 wins over their respective opponents. With both defending champions Mizoram boys and Telangana girls failing to qualify for the Inter-Zonals, the titles were up for grabs. In the finals, Karnataka defeated Assam 2-0 while Tamil Nadu girls got the better of last edition silver medallist Delhi 2-0. In the girls’ team final, 2025 Asian Under-17 girls singles champion Diksha SR gave Tamil Nadu a winning start as she defeated Rishika Nandi 15-12, 15-12. The women’s doubles combination of Ananya Arun and Anjana Manikandan then sealed the victory with a 16-14, 12-15, 15-10 lead over Nandi and Ishita Negi. The men’s singles final saw Hardik Divyansh defeat 2023 Asian U-15 champion Bornil Changmai. The formidable combination of Pavan and Punith Suresh then got the better of Changmai and Aanayan Borah 9-15, 15-10, 7-15 to clinch the crown. RESULTS Boys U-19: Karnataka bt Assam 2-0 (Hardik Divyansh bt Bornil Changmai 18-16, 15-6; Pavan Suresh/Punith Suresh bt Aanayan Borah/Changmai 15-9, 10-15, 15-7) Girls U-19: Tamil Nadu bt Delhi 2-0 (Diksha SR bt Rishika Nandi 15-12, 15-12; Ananya Arun/Anjana Manikandan bt Nandi/Ishita Negi 16-14, 12-15, 15-10) -Team Sportstar MOTORSPORTS Dramatic opening day of National Car Racing Championship The opening day of round 2 of the CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship was dramatic in nature, filled with late changes and overtakes. Augustine Boby edged Shatveer Shetty by a mere 0.032 seconds in the F1300 Novice Cup here on Sunday. Mehul Agarwal produced a late overtake to beat teammate Arya Singh by 0.237 seconds in LGB Formula 4, while Deepak Ravikumar staged a remarkable recovery from 15th after an early stall to win the second Indian Junior Touring Cars race by 0.308 seconds. Srinivas Teja had won the opening race in the category. In the other categories, Bengaluru’s Anish Shetty won the Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup Pro race, while Vadodara’s Kabir Sahoch continued his winning run in the amateur class despite two red-flag interruptions at the Kari Motor Speedway. Mumbai’s Pratik Sonawane completed a double in the gentleman class of the JK Tyre Levitas Cup, while Arjun Narendran won the Indian Super Touring Cars race and Balaprasath A triumphed in Indian Touring Cars. Diljith T S also secured a double in Super Stock. The Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup amateur race witnessed further drama with a last-lap collision between Paramjeet Singh and Pushpendra Kumar Markandey, allowing Brandon Dsouza to climb from ninth on the grid to third. Action concludes on Sunday with the final day of round 2. -Team Sportstar MORE SPORTS Six cities across Telangana to host the Khelo India Youth Games 2026 The logo and mascot for the eighth edition of Khelo India Youth Games were unveiled on Sunday by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A Revanath Reddy. The tournament is going to be played across six cities in Telangana: Hyderabad, Khammam, Karimnagar, Hanumakonda, Mahabubnagar and Nizamabad, between December 11 and 22. Around 8000 athletes are expected to participate in the event. “The Union Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, is committed to promoting sports. Various competitions, including the Khelo India Youth Games, Beach Games, Winter Games and Tribal Games, are being organised under the Khelo India initiative to encourage greater participation of the younger generation in sports,” said Mandaviya. This time, the tournament will have 29 events, including two demonstration events: sailing and karra samu. Softball will also make its debut as a competitive sport in the tournament. -Team Sportstar With inputs from PTI CHESS Final day of Maharashtra State Schools Chess Championship 2026 Veer Dhaval Shah and AIM Hriday Maniar produced outstanding performances, winning all seven games in their respective categories, as the Maharashtra State Schools Chess Championship 2026 concluded at Rustomjee Cambridge International School, Dahisar (West), on Sunday. The three-day championship, organised by Indian Chess School, witnessed keen competition among 387 players across six FIDE-rated categories in the Under-9, Under-13 and Under-17 Open and Girls sections. In the Under-9 Open category, Veer Dhaval Shah (1501) of Jamnabai Narsee School, JVPD, emerged as the undisputed champion with a perfect score of seven points from seven rounds. Ivaan Dubey (1545), who had earlier won the Under-7 Open title in the first stage, secured second place with six points, while Aarav Ravi Jhavar (1571) of Jamnabai Narsee School finished third with six points. The Under-9 Girls category witnessed an exciting three-way finish, with Lavanya Singh (1448) of Sanjivani International School emerging champion with six points on superior tie-break. Ishi Singh (1538) of J. B. Petit High School for Girls also scored six points to secure second place, while Nikita Sandeep (1411) finished third with six points. In the Under-13 Open category, Vihaan Anupam Agrawal (1858) of Narayana Olympiad School emerged champion with six points from seven rounds, edging out top seed Nirvaan Nirav Shah (1956) of Don Bosco International School, who also scored six points but had to settle for second place on tie-break. In the Under-13 Girls category, Tisyaa Apurva Patt (1524) of Avalon Heights International School produced an impressive performance to clinch the championship with six points from seven rounds. Pranitha Bhava (1655) of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan Vidyalaya secured second place with 5.5 points. The Under-17 Open category witnessed a commanding performance by top seed AIM Hriday Maniar (1910), who maintained his winning streak throughout the championship to secure the title with a perfect score of seven points from seven rounds. Shaurya Ashish Modi (1626) finished second with 5.5 points, while Soham Sudarshan Sahamate (1667) secured third place, also with 5.5 points. In the Under-17 Girls category, top seed Drishya Naik (1713) emerged as a convincing champion with 6.5 points from seven rounds, finishing 1.5 points ahead of her nearest challengers. The championship served as the selection tournament for the National Schools Chess Championship, scheduled to be held in Ahmedabad from December 16 to 20, 2026. The top two finishers in each of the six categories have earned the opportunity to represent Maharashtra at the national championship. -Team Sportstar RESULTS Boys U-19: Karnataka bt Assam 2-0 (Hardik Divyansh bt Bornil Changmai 18-16, 15-6; Pavan Suresh/Punith Suresh bt Aanayan Borah/Changmai 15-9, 10-15, 15-7) Girls U-19: Tamil Nadu bt Delhi 2-0 (Diksha SR bt Rishika Nandi 15-12, 15-12; Ananya Arun/Anjana Manikandan bt Nandi/Ishita Negi 16-14, 12-15, 15-10)

articles.content: CHENNAI MOTORSPORT Atiqa Mir only Indian chosen for FIA’s women driver development program Indian racing prodigy Atiqa Mir is among nine drivers chosen worldwide in the junior category for the FIA Girls On Track Rising Stars program for 2026. Atiqa is one of the youngest drivers chosen for the world body FIA backed initiative aimed at promoting and developing young women drivers at the grassroots level. She is also is the only Indian named in the age 12-14 junior category. Girls On Track was launched by the FIA in 2018. Atiqa’s selection follows a string of impressive performances in the Champions of the Future Academy (COTFA) championship and the FIA Karting World Championship where she finished sixth in the opening race. She had dominated the COTFA round in Greece earlier this year. “In just over two weeks, nine talented racers will head to Cremona Circuit (in Italy) for three-day training camp designed to sharpen their skills and help take their racing to the next level,” read a note from the FIA Women in Motorsport Commission. The other drivers picked by the FIA in the junior category are Lina Salamanca from France, Sofia Calderon from Costa Rica, Cora Moore from Britain, Anna Regina Franco Rodriguez from Mexico, Lily Rizk from Egypt, Kira Maistrenko from Ukraine, Annais Orelana from Chile and Emily Grace Hamer from Australia. Atiqa, the first Indian to be backed by the Formula 1 Academy, is currently taking part in the final round of COTFA series in Franciacorta, Italy. - PTI CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship, Round 2: Photo finish, last-lap battles and dramatic comebacks mark opening day DTS Racing’s Augustine Boby edged Meco Racing’s Shatveer Shetty by just 0.032 seconds in the F1300 Novice Cup, while Dark Don Racing’s Mehul Agarwal and Team Performance Racing’s Deepak Ravikumar pulled off late overtakes to claim victories in LGB Formula 4 and Indian Junior Touring Cars, respectively on the opening day of Round 2 of the CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship at the Kari Motor Speedway in Coimbatore. Vadodara’s Kabir Sahoch continued his winning run in the Amateur class, surviving two red-flag interruptions and a six-lap restart to finish 0.979 seconds ahead of Saurav Sanjay Dey in the Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup. In the JK Tyre Levitas Cup, Mumbai’s Pratik Sonawane completed a double in the Gentleman class with two pole-to-flag victories. In the Super Saloon categories, Arka Motorsports’ Arjun Narendran won the Indian Super Touring Cars race by 7.288 seconds after holding off an early challenge from Arjun Balu, while Team N1 Intervalve’s Biren Pithawalla snatched second from Balu in the closing moments. In the Indian Touring Cars, Team Performance Racing’s Balaprasath A won ahead of Ramcharan Chandran and Vidyaprakash Damodaran. - Team Sportstar GOLF Women’s Pro Golf Tour, 14th leg: Jasmine Shekar wins second title of season, holds off Vani and Ridhima Jasmine Shekar managed to extend her overnight one-shot advantage to two shots and claim her second title of the season in the 14th leg of the Women’s Pro Golf Tour at the Rambagh Golf Club in Jaipur on Saturday. The 21-year-old Jasmine, who hails from Bengaluru, took the lead into the final round, held her nerve to card 1-over 71 and finish ahead of two of the most experienced players in India, Vani Kapoor (72) and Ridhima Dilawari (74). In a week when no player had an under par total, Jasmine aggregated 5-over with rounds of 74-70-71, while Vani Kapoor (75-70-72) was 7-over for three days and Ridhima (74-71-74) was 9-over at the challenging course. Shweta Mansingh (74-75-71) was fourth at 10-over for three days. Jasmine has been one of the consistent performers on the domestic circuit, more so this year. She had opened her 2026 campaign with a victory in the first leg in Mumbai and had since come close to adding to that tally, finishing runner-up at both DLF Golf & Country Club and Jaypee Wishtown. At Rambagh, she finally converted another opportunity into a title. She became the third player after Ridhima and Vani to win more than once in 2026. The result was particularly satisfying because the challenge came from two players who have enjoyed outstanding seasons. Vani and Ridhima had shared second place going into the final round, and both had the experience and form to put Jasmine under pressure. Vani had also arrived in Jaipur on the back of an impressive runner-up finish at the Hero Women’s Indian Open, the best result of her Ladies European Tour career. Jasmine, however, did just enough to give herself a chance and convert it into a fine win. The Rambagh Golf Club course, a par-70 layout, proved a demanding test throughout the week. Scoring was difficult, with players finding it hard to get into red figures. In fact, there was just one under-par round in the entire tournament, a superb four-under 66 by Tvesa Malik. Despite producing the lowest round of the week, Tvesa could finish only tied seventh, underlining the difficulty of the conditions. She was tied seventh with Ananya Datar, a first-round co-leader with amateur Ojaswani Saraswat (74), who was tied fifth alongside Riya Jadon. Jasmine played solid on the final day and was steady. She had two bogeys on the second and fifth, which put her in danger. However she had a birdie on the Par-3 sixth followed by five straight pars. Another birdie on the 12th was followed by four more pars. She looked set for the win as she stayed ahead of Vani. She could even afford a bogey on the 17th. Vani had two bogeys and no birdies on the front and on the back nine she had just one birdie, but she also bogeyed the 18th. A birdie on the 18th could have got her into a play-off, but it was not to be and she lost by two. For Vani, second place was another strong result in a season in which she has remained one of the leading forces on the domestic circuit. The experienced professional has already won twice this year and finished runner-up on three occasions before the Jaipur event. Her recent performance at the Hero Women’s Indian Open had further underlined her ability to compete at a higher level. Ridhima, meanwhile, continued to add valuable points to an already impressive season. The Order of Merit leader has been the most consistent player on the tour, with four victories before this event, and her third-place finish keeps her firmly in position to win the Merit honours. Though the result at the Jaipur leg looked close, this week belonged to Jasmine, who never let things get out of hand and the next event, which will be the final one for 2026, will be held at Noida Jaypee Wishtown, which had also hosted the sixth leg, which was won by Ridhima and Jasmine was second. - PTI Top golfers for PGTI event at Digboi Top Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI) golfers such as Honey Baisoya, Om Prakash Chouhan, Akshay Sharma and Rashid Khan will be seen in action in the ₹1 crore Indian Oil Servo Masters event to be held at the Digboi Golf Links course, Assam, from November 17 to 20. The tournament week will begin with the pro-am event on Sunday. - Team Sportstar SNOOKER Six Indians advance to final stage of World Snooker Championships Kamal Chawla outplayed Laxman Rawat to book his spot in the final stage of the IBSF World Snooker Championships in Indore on Saturday. On song from the get-go, Chawla scored a crushing 4-1 victory in the third round of the first event. A little later, five more Indian cueists booked their spots in the second stage with contrasting victories. After the two split the first two frames of the best-of-seven-frame clash, Chawla shifted gears to leave Rawat gasping in his wake. He made a brilliant 133 break in the third frame, and after winning the fourth on the black, the 47-year-old came up with a sizzling break of 108 to power into the second stage. In the clash between two promising cueists, Kreishh Gurbaxani came good when it mattered to score a gritty 4-2 win over the red-hot Rayaan Razmi. Gurbaxani, who played two seasons on the pro tour, got going after losing the first two frames. A fine break of 78 in the third gave him the confidence, and he played a solid game to keep Razmi in check, winning the next three frames, which could have gone either way. S Shrikrishna, a former World champion in the shorter format, came into his own after a slow start against fellow Indian Pushpender Singh. After losing the first frame, Shrikrishna had runs of 81, 84 and 120 on his way to a 4-1 victory. Piyush Kushwaha, Ranveer Duggal and Digvijay Kadian were other Indians to advance to the final stage. - PTI MORE SPORTS Ladakh Marathon adds 180 km Siachen Ultra to race roster The Ladakh Marathon is taking high-altitude distance running to new extremes with the launch of the Siachen Ultra, conceived as the world’s toughest ultra-running challenge across 111 miles (180 km) of the Trans-Himalayan ranges. The race will traverse the mountain landscape of the Karakoram and Himalaya, taking field of highly experienced ultra runners from Warshi Village near Siachen to Leh, via the Nubra region and Khardung La at 17,618 ft (5,370 m). The race is dedicated to the courage, service and sacrifice of the Indian Army in Siachen. A strict 30-hour cutoff will require runners to maintain a demanding pace through the day and night, across exposed desert stretches, long climbs and potentially sub-zero temperatures and strong winds at the pass. Given the exceptional demands of the route, participation will be restricted to ultra runners whose experience and preparation meet the Ladakh Marathon’s stringent eligibility criteria. - Team Sportstar

articles.content: Maharashtra Farmers Update: महाराष्ट्रातील शेती आणि शेतकऱ्यांना तंत्रज्ञानाच्या माध्यमातून अधिक सक्षम करण्यासाठी राज्य सरकारने एक महत्त्वपूर्ण पाऊल उचलले आहे. कृषी उन्नती योजनेंतर्गत 'डिजिटल अॅग्रिकल्चर मिशन' (अॅग्रिस्टॅक) साठी सन २०२६-२७ या आर्थिक वर्षातील दुसऱ्या हफ्त्याचा निधी वितरीत करण्यास अधिकृत मंजुरी देण्यात आली आहे. यासंदर्भात कृषी विभागाने २७ ऑक्टोबर २०२६ रोजी सविस्तर शासन निर्णय जारी केला आहे. (Good News for Maharashtra Farmers: Government Releases Second Installment of Funds for Digital Agriculture Mission).किती निधी झाला मंजूर?डिजिटल क्रॉप सर्व्हे (DCS) या महत्त्वाच्या घटकासाठी केंद्र आणि राज्य सरकारचा हिस्सा मिळून एकूण २० कोटी ५ लाख ८० हजार रुपये (₹२०,०५,८०,०००/-) इतका निधी कृषी आयुक्तालयाकडे वर्ग करण्यात येत आहे. यामध्ये केंद्र शासनाचा ६०% हिस्सा (१२,०३,४८,००० रुपये) आणि राज्य शासनाचा ४०% समरूप हिस्सा (८,०२,३२,००० रुपये) समाविष्ट आहे.प्रवर्गनिहाय निधीचे वाटप खालीलप्रमाणे:सर्वसाधारण प्रवर्ग: ₹ १५,८१,१७,२१३/-अनुसूचित जाती प्रवर्ग (SC): ₹ २,३७,०८,५५७/-अनुसूचित जमाती प्रवर्ग (ST): ₹ १,८७,५४,२३०/- .Good News : मोठी बातमी !एसटी कर्मचाऱ्यांसाठी गुड न्यूज, दिवाळीपूर्वी वेतनाचा मार्ग मोकळा .योजनेचा उद्देश काय?डिजिटल क्रॉप सर्व्हे या डिजिटल उपक्रमामुळे राज्यातील पिकांची पाहणी (Digital Crop Survey) अधिक अचूक आणि पारदर्शक होणार आहे. तसेच, शासकीय योजनांचा लाभ थेट पात्र शेतकऱ्यांपर्यंत पोहोचवणे यामुळे सोपे होणार आहे. सदर निधी पुणे येथील कृषी आयुक्तांच्या नियंत्रणाखाली सर्व वित्तीय नियम व पारदर्शकता बाळगून खर्च करण्याचे निर्देश शासनाने दिले आहेत..सकाळ+चे सदस्य व्हाशॉपिंगसाठी 'सकाळ प्राईम डील्स'च्या भन्नाट ऑफर्स पाहण्यासाठी क्लिक करा.Read Marathi news and watch Live TV.
